drugs.name: Teplizumab
drugs.mechanism: Fc-engineered humanized anti-CD3 monoclonal antibody deactivating autoreactive T lymphocytes and increasing regulatory T cells
drugs.efficacy: Delays clinical onset of Stage 3 Type 1 Diabetes by a median of 2 to 3 years in high-risk Stage 2 patients
drugs.adverse_effects: Lymphopenia, cytokine release syndrome, rash, headache, transient transaminase elevation

drugs.name: Insulin Glargine
drugs.mechanism: Long-acting basal insulin providing peakless 24-hour glycemic control by stimulating peripheral glucose uptake
drugs.efficacy: Cornerstone basal insulin regimen for intensive glycemic replacement therapy
drugs.adverse_effects: Hypoglycemia, weight gain, injection site lipodystrophy, localized allergic reactions

drugs.name: Insulin Aspart
drugs.mechanism: Rapid-acting prandial insulin with fast monomeric absorption controlling postprandial glucose excursions
drugs.efficacy: Rapid onset and shorter duration matching physiological mealtime insulin requirements
drugs.adverse_effects: Hypoglycemia, weight gain, local injection reactions

drugs.name: Insulin Lispro
drugs.mechanism: Rapid-acting prandial insulin analog binding the insulin receptor with fast absorption kinetics for mealtime glycemic management
drugs.efficacy: Rapid prandial glycemic control with reduced late postprandial hypoglycemia

drugs.name: Insulin Degludec
drugs.mechanism: Forms multi-hexamer chains in subcutaneous tissue delivering ultra-flat, peakless 42+ hour basal insulin release
drugs.efficacy: Provides flexible basal dosing with significantly reduced nocturnal hypoglycemia rates
drugs.adverse_effects: Hypoglycemia, weight gain, injection site reactions

drugs.name: Pramlintide
drugs.mechanism: Synthetic analogue of human amylin slowing gastric emptying, suppressing glucagon, and increasing satiety
drugs.efficacy: Reduces postprandial glucose spikes and total required prandial insulin dose
drugs.adverse_effects: Severe hypoglycemia risk when combined with insulin, nausea, vomiting, anorexia

drugs.name: Abatacept
drugs.mechanism: Binds CD80 and CD86 on APCs to block CD28 co-stimulation required for autoimmune T cell activation
drugs.approval: Investigational in T1D / FDA Approved in RA
drugs.efficacy: Slows decline of C-peptide secretion during initial 2 years of clinical onset
drugs.adverse_effects: Headache, upper respiratory tract infections, nausea, infusion reactions

drugs.name: Rituximab
drugs.mechanism: Chimeric monoclonal antibody targeting CD20 to deplete mature B lymphocytes and disrupt autoantibody presentation
drugs.approval: Investigational in T1D / FDA Approved in RA/Lymphoma
drugs.efficacy: Preserved C-peptide beta-cell function for 1 year in newly diagnosed T1D patients
drugs.adverse_effects: Infusion reactions, lymphopenia, hypogammaglobulinemia, infection risk

drugs.name: Otelixizumab
drugs.mechanism: Chimeric humanized anti-CD3 monoclonal antibody modulating TCR-CD3 complex signalling
drugs.efficacy: Preserved C-peptide secretion in Phase 2 trial of new-onset T1D
drugs.adverse_effects: EBV reactivation at higher doses, flu-like symptoms, cytokine release

drugs.name: Golimumab
drugs.mechanism: Human anti-TNF-alpha monoclonal antibody neutralizing soluble and transmembrane TNF to protect beta-islets
drugs.approval: Investigational in T1D / FDA Approved in RA/UC
drugs.efficacy: Preserved endogenous insulin production and reduced exogenous insulin requirements in T1D clinical trial

drugs.name: Alefacept
drugs.mechanism: Dimers of CD2-binding portion of LFA-3 fused to IgG1 Fc, selectively depleting memory T cells
drugs.efficacy: Preserved C-peptide secretion and reduced hypoglycemia in new-onset T1D (T1DAL study)

drugs.name: Anti-Thymocyte Globulin (Low-Dose ATG)
drugs.target: T cell surface antigens (CD2, CD3, CD4, CD8, CD28)
drugs.mechanism: Induces selective T-cell depletion followed by preferential Treg reconstitution in autoimmune diabetes
drugs.approval: Investigational in T1D / FDA Approved in Transplant
drugs.efficacy: Preserved beta-cell function and improved HbA1c in established and new-onset T1D
drugs.adverse_effects: Cytokine release syndrome, serum sickness, leukopenia, thrombocytopenia

drugs.name: Low-Dose Interleukin-2 (Aldesleukin)
drugs.mechanism: Selectively stimulates CD4+CD25+FOXP3+ regulatory T cells via high-affinity IL-2 receptor without activating effector cells
drugs.efficacy: Selectively expands functional regulatory T cells in patients with type 1 diabetes (DF-IL2 trial)
drugs.adverse_effects: Injection site pain, mild transient flu-like symptoms

drugs.name: Verapamil
drugs.type: Small molecule L-type calcium channel blocker
drugs.mechanism: Downregulates beta-cell TXNIP expression and protects beta cells from apoptosis and oxidative stress
drugs.approval: Repurposed in T1D / FDA Approved in Hypertension
drugs.efficacy: Maintains endogenous C-peptide beta cell function over 1 and 2 years in adults and children with newly diagnosed T1D

drugs.name: Diamyd (GAD-Alum)
drugs.mechanism: Formulation of recombinant human GAD65 with aluminium hydroxide inducing immune tolerance to beta-cell autoantigens
drugs.efficacy: Preserves endogenous insulin secretion in HLA-DR3-DQ2 genotype positive newly diagnosed T1D patients
drugs.adverse_effects: Localized lymph node tenderness, mild transient injection site reactions

drugs.name: Ustekinumab
drugs.target: IL12B (p40 subunit of IL-12 and IL-23)
drugs.mechanism: Human monoclonal antibody binding IL-12/23 p40 subunit, blocking Th1 and Th17 cell differentiation and cytokine production
drugs.approval: Investigational in T1D / FDA Approved in Psoriasis/Crohn's
drugs.efficacy: Preserved C-peptide secretion and lowered insulin dose requirements in recent-onset T1D (USTE1D trial)
drugs.adverse_effects: Upper respiratory infections, headache, fatigue, injection site erythema
